story_description: Parse and normalize the event stream from Codex app-server into NormalizedEvent types that the Blaze UI and hook system can consume, bridging the JSON-RPC protocol differences from the NDJSON format used by Claude Code.
task_description: Create CodexJSONRPCParser that reads raw JSON from app-server stdout and classifies each message as response, request, or notification based on JSON-RPC 2.0 field presence rules.
atom_description: Implement CodexJSONRPCParser struct that parses newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 messages, classifies them by type (response, request, notification), and routes them appropriately: responses to pending request handlers, requests to approval callback, and notifications to the event stream.
problem_statement: Codex app-server emits JSON-RPC 2.0 messages over stdio (newline-delimited JSON), not the NDJSON event stream format used by Claude Code. The JSON-RPC 2.0 spec defines three message types distinguished by field presence: responses have id + result or error, requests have id + method, and notifications have method but no id. Blaze needs a parser that correctly discriminates these message types and routes them to appropriate handlers. Malformed JSON must be handled gracefully without crashing.

assumptions: App-server emits one JSON object per line (newline-delimited)
JSON-RPC 2.0 message format is stable across Codex versions
Field presence rules match JSON-RPC 2.0 spec exactly
Method names follow dot-notation hierarchy (turn/started, item/agentMessage/delta)
Result and error fields are mutually exclusive in responses
Params field is optional for both requests and notifications
constraints: Parser must be synchronous and stateless for thread-safety
Must handle partial or truncated JSON gracefully
Must not crash on unexpected field types or missing fields
Must preserve original JSON for logging and debugging
No third-party JSON parsing libraries; use Foundation JSONDecoder only
Must support all Codex method names discovered in CodexMonitor
functional_requirements: FR1: Parser shall accept a single line string and return a parsed JSONRPCMessage or ParseError
FR2: Parser shall classify message as response when id is present AND (result OR error is present)
FR3: Parser shall classify message as request when id is present AND method is present AND result/error are absent
FR4: Parser shall classify message as notification when method is present AND id is absent
FR5: Parser shall extract method name as String for requests and notifications
FR6: Parser shall extract id as either Int or String to match JSON-RPC 2.0 flexibility
FR7: Parser shall extract params as AnyCodable for downstream processing
FR8: Parser shall extract result as AnyCodable for response payloads
FR9: Parser shall extract error.code (Int), error.message (String), and error.data (AnyCodable?) for error responses
FR10: Parser shall return ParseError.invalidJSON when input is not valid JSON
FR11: Parser shall return ParseError.ambiguousMessage when classification rules are not met
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Parse latency shall be under 1ms for typical messages (under 10KB)
NFR2: Parser shall handle messages up to 1MB without memory issues
NFR3: Parser shall not allocate excessive memory for malformed input
NFR4: Parser must be thread-safe (stateless design)
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create new file CodexJSONRPCParser.swift in Blaze/Sources/Engine/Codex/ directory
Step 2: Define JSONRPCMessageType enum with cases: response, request, notification
Step 3: Define JSONRPCError struct with code (Int), message (String), data (AnyCodable?) properties
Step 4: Define JSONRPCMessage struct with type (JSONRPCMessageType), id (JSONRPCId?), method (String?), params (AnyCodable?), result (AnyCodable?), error (JSONRPCError?) properties
Step 5: Define JSONRPCId enum with cases: int(Int), string(String) to handle both id types
Step 6: Define ParseError enum with cases: invalidJSON(String), ambiguousMessage(String)
Step 7: Implement JSONRPCId Codable conformance to decode from Int or String
Step 8: Implement CodexJSONRPCParser struct with static parse(line: String) throws -> JSONRPCMessage method
Step 9: In parse(), first decode line as [String: AnyCodable] to inspect raw fields
Step 10: Extract id field, checking for Int or String type
Step 11: Check for result or error field presence to identify responses
Step 12: Check for method field presence to identify requests/notifications
Step 13: Apply classification rules: id + (result|error) = response, id + method = request, method alone = notification
Step 14: If no classification matches, throw ParseError.ambiguousMessage with field summary
Step 15: Construct and return JSONRPCMessage with all extracted fields
Step 16: Add parseError convenience that returns nil for invalid JSON instead of throwing
Step 17: Write comprehensive unit tests for all message types and edge cases

edge_cases: Edge case 1: Empty string input - throws ParseError.invalidJSON
Edge case 2: Valid JSON but empty object {} - throws ParseError.ambiguousMessage
Edge case 3: Response with both result and error - classified as response, error takes precedence
Edge case 4: Message with id as Int (123) - extracted as JSONRPCId.int(123)
Edge case 5: Message with id as String (abc-123) - extracted as JSONRPCId.string(abc-123)
Edge case 6: Message with id as null - treated as no id (notification if method present)
Edge case 7: Notification with extra unknown fields - parsed successfully, extra fields ignored
Edge case 8: Method name with slashes (item/agentMessage/delta) - preserved exactly as string
Edge case 9: Very large params object (1MB JSON) - parsed if valid, may be slow
Edge case 10: Unicode in method name or string values - handled by JSONDecoder
Edge case 11: Trailing whitespace or newline - trimmed before parsing
Edge case 12: Multiple JSON objects on same line - only first is parsed
failure_modes: FM1: Invalid JSON syntax - returns ParseError.invalidJSON with decoder error message
FM2: Unexpected field types (id as array) - returns ParseError.ambiguousMessage
FM3: Memory exhaustion on huge input - limited by JSONDecoder, fails gracefully
FM4: Stack overflow on deeply nested JSON - limited by JSONDecoder recursion
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/Engine/Codex/CodexJSONRPCParser.swift file. Remove imports from dependent files. Parser is stateless with no persistence, rollback is trivial.
